citations.quote: An integrated systems-level model for propulsion, spacecraft (power, data, telecommunication, thermal management), and orbit and attitude maneuvers is developed to support solution space exploration.

The goal of this study is to establish the optimal performance parameters for future MEP technology that are applicable to a broad range of flight demonstration platforms (e.g. dedicated 3-12U CubeSats to ESPA-class spacecraft ), for a variety of applications, including LEO and Earth escape orbit transfers, travel to interplanetary destinations, hover and drag make-up missions, and performing reaction wheel-free attitude control.

First, we develop parametric analytic systems-level integrated models for propulsion, attitude control, power, telecommunication, and thermal, which are key elements in small spacecraft design. The models include appropriate mass, power, and size scaling laws for propulsion, power, and thermal subsystems.

Furthermore, typical existing CubeSats do not usually operate at the high power or high voltage levels required to support propulsion systems, nor do they have solutions for managing the resulting high thermal loads (most existing CubeSats rely on passive thermal control).
Although this work focuses on MEP for small spacecraft form-factor, the models and approach are applicable to other propulsion technologies and larger spacecraft architectures.

A systems-level model is essential to capture all interacting dynamics and constraints of this problem, particularly because small spacecraft are highly-constrained and are extremely resource-constrained. The multidisciplinary integrated model consists of analytic representations of the propulsion system, orbital dynamics, energy collection and management system, and thermal management system.
